rationale: This meta-regression synthesizes 23 studies in the institutional economics of macro Water Resource Management (WRM), estimating an aggregate 'water institution-performance effect' (including primary studies that use aspects of water law and policy themselves to capture performance) aimed at lowering transaction costs in WRM. Neither the title nor the abstract addresses household or community drinking water or sanitation service delivery (failing C1, E07) or disaggregates household/community water or sanitation access, connection, coverage, reliability, quality, or affordability outcomes (failing C4).
plain_vs_narrow_note: Under the literal/plain Criterion 2 wording, the study qualifies on exposure (c2_legal_admin_plain = yes) because it analyses macro water institutions, water laws, policies, and administration; under the narrow reading (c2_legal_admin_narrow = no), it examines aggregate macro-institutional WRM indices and transaction costs rather than concrete legal or administrative mechanisms governing household/community service access. Under both readings, however, the record is excluded because it concerns macro Water Resource Management rather than household or community water/sanitation service access (C1) and synthesizes generic institutional performance rather than service access outcomes (C4).

evidence_quotes.quote: A Meta-Analysis of Water Institutions and Their Performance: Implications for Water Resource Management
This pioneering study synthesizes and quantifies the overall water institution-performance effect using data extracted from 23 original studies.
strengthening of water laws, policies, and administration to lower transaction costs in the water space.
